s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive symmetric small joint pain with morning stiffness and fatigue
salient_findings: Symmetric pain in small joints of hands, wrists, knees, and ankles
Early morning stiffness lasting 2 hours daily
Severe fatigue throughout the day
Recent mild COVID-19 infection
Elevated rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody
Synovitis and tenosynovitis on MRI
key_facts: 4 months of progressively worsening symptoms
Symmetric joint pain
Early morning stiffness lasting 2 hours daily
Severe fatigue throughout the day
Recent mild COVID-19 infection confirmed by SARS-CoV-2 PCR
No recent genitourinary or gastrointestinal infections
No history of psoriasis or uveitis
Family history of rheumatoid arthritis
Elevated rheumatoid factor (62.29 IU/mL)
Elevated anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody (237.39 units)
Normal erythrocyte sedimentation rate (13 mm/hour) and C-reactive protein (4.3 mg/L)
Antinuclear antibody titer of 1:640
Negative extractable nuclear antigen and double-stranded DNA antibodies
No joint erosion on hand ultrasound
Synovitis and tenosynovitis on MRI of the hands

shortlist.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, symmetric joint pain, morning stiffness, and family history of rheumatoid arthritis

shortlist.label: Seropositive Rheumatoid Arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, consistent with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis

shortlist.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
shortlist.why_kept: Antinuclear antibody titer of 1:640, although extractable nuclear antigen and double-stranded DNA antibodies were negative

shortlist.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
shortlist.why_kept: Overlap of symptoms and laboratory findings, including elevated antinuclear antibody titer and rheumatoid factor

shortlist.label: COVID-19 associated arthritis
shortlist.why_kept: Recent mild COVID-19 infection, which may be a triggering factor for arthritis

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of symmetric joint pain, early morning stiffness, and severe fatigue, combined with elevated rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody, are consistent with seropositive rheumatoid arthritis. The presence of synovitis and tenosynovitis on MRI also supports this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Rheumatoid Arthritis
rejected.why: While the patient's symptoms are consistent with rheumatoid arthritis, the presence of seropositive markers (elevated rheumatoid factor and anti-cyclic citrullinated peptide antibody) makes seropositive rheumatoid arthritis a more specific diagnosis.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient's antinuclear antibody titer is elevated, but extractable nuclear antigen and double-stranded DNA antibodies are negative, making this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Mixed Connective Tissue Disease
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not meet the criteria for mixed connective tissue disease, which typically includes a combination of features from multiple autoimmune diseases.

rejected.label: COVID-19 associated arthritis
rejected.why: While the patient had a recent COVID-19 infection, the duration and nature of her symptoms are more consistent with a chronic autoimmune condition like seropositive rheumatoid arthritis rather than a post-infectious arthritis.

rejected.label: Systemic Lupus Erythematosus
rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results do not meet the criteria for systemic lupus erythematosus.
